hypotheses.claim: At least one of four pre-declared signals (mom_h, vwap_dev, or_pos, rvol_ratio) measured on NIFTY 1-minute index bars carries directional information about the forward h-minute index return at h in {5,15,30,60}, strongly enough to matter economically at Amendment E's capital. Specifically: some (signal, horizon) cell shows a Spearman IC whose |t| clears the Section 4 noise bar for N=16 (|t| >= 2.36), with the SAME IC sign in each of the four calendar years measured separately (2022 partial, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 partial — Amendment D5's sign-consistency rule applied to time rather than liquidity era), AND whose implied gross edge per trade at that horizon is at least 2x the net per-trade target from Amendment E5. Direction is NOT predicted: both momentum (IC>0) and reversal (IC<0) count, which is why the bar is two-sided and the sign-consistency requirement is what stops a sign flip across years being read as a finding.
hypotheses.kill_criterion: KILLED if no (signal, horizon) cell satisfies all three conditions together: (a) |t| >= 2.36 on the pooled Spearman IC, (b) the same IC sign in every calendar year with at least 60 trading days of data, and (c) implied gross edge per trade >= 2x the Amendment E5 net target at that horizon's achievable trade frequency. A cell that clears (a) but fails (b) is a sign-unstable estimate and is NOT a finding — that is the D5 lesson. A cell that clears (a) and (b) but fails (c) is real but too small to trade at this capital, and is recorded as such rather than carried forward. This screen can only kill or advance; per Amendment B5 it cannot promote anything.

signals.mom_h: return over the trailing h minutes (momentum if IC>0, reversal if IC<0)
signals.vwap_dev: (price - session VWAP) / trailing 30-min stdev of price
signals.or_pos: position in the first-15-min opening range: (p - OR_low)/(OR_high - OR_low)
signals.rvol_ratio: trailing 30-min realised vol / that session's median 30-min realised vol

hypotheses.note: Arena 5, screen 1, and the RESUME.md Step-4 'measure before building' item. Runs on data/intraday/NIFTY/index.parquet (370,626 1-min bars, 992 trading days, 2022-08-16..2026-08-14), archived from Dhan on 2026-08-14. gate='strict' is recorded for form only: this screen computes correlations on index bars and executes no fills, so no liquidity gate applies to it. Any STRATEGY descending from a surviving cell must be re-run under a real gate. equity is registered at the BOTTOM of Amendment E's Rs 50k-1L range, which is the conservative choice for the economic condition (c). Killing this hypothesis does not by itself close arena 'intraday_index' — Section 7 leaves arena closure an operator decision recorded with its grounds, and Section 8 fixes no screen allotment. It would, however, close the specific idea that a single unconditional signal predicts intraday index direction.

detail.why_killed: Conditions (a) and (b) both PASSED for 8 of 16 cells: the ICs are statistically significant after correcting for the overlap of forward windows, and sign-stable in all five calendar years. The kill is entirely on (c). The best cells (vwap_dev and or_pos at h=60, IC ~0.053) imply a 3.0-index-point expected move, worth Rs ~97 gross on one lot at delta 0.5 — against Rs 147 of round-trip cost at the project's registered 0.75/leg spread. Breakeven needs a spread under ~Rs 0.36/leg, about 1.9% of a Rs 19 option, which is tighter than NIFTY's cheap-option book actually quotes. At ZERO spread the same cells net only Rs ~48, and every cell at h<=30 loses money even then.
detail.measured_absence_not_absent_evidence: This is a measured absence, like Arena 1 and Arena 4, not an absence of evidence. The predictability is REAL and stable across four years; it is simply smaller than the bid-ask spread. Nothing here suggests looking harder at the same signals would help — a larger sample would only measure the same too-small effect more precisely.
detail.biases_favour_the_dead_hypothesis: Every approximation in the translation biases the estimate UPWARD, so the true edge is smaller than the number that failed: (i) it assumes a full position on every signal, ignoring the E[|z|]~0.8 factor for signal strength; (ii) it holds delta constant at 0.5 and charges no theta over the 60-minute hold; (iii) it charges no market impact. The kill is therefore conservative.
detail.artifact_found_and_removed: A fourth signal, rvol_ratio, initially produced the strongest result in the screen (IC 0.084, t 5.75, sign-consistent across all years). It was pure lookahead: its normaliser was the session median of realised vol, computed over the WHOLE session, so the 10:00 value knew 15:00. With an expanding (past-only) median it fails condition (a) at every horizon and disappears from the screen entirely. Recorded because it is exactly the kind of result that would have been reported as a discovery.
detail.not_tested_here: This screen tests UNCONDITIONAL single signals. It does not test conditional or interaction effects, nor does it test whether a larger per-trade edge exists at horizons beyond 60 minutes. Those would be separate registrations against a fresh comparisons budget.

futures_trend.grounds: Closed on resolvability and throughput, NOT on demonstrated absence of edge. T2 established the arena is not structurally capped: the perfect-foresight oracle reaches Sharpe 8.9, friction is irrelevant, and N_eff 2.59 does not prevent an 8-name book reaching 1.0 — IC ~0.05 would suffice. What closes it is that the question cannot be answered with the data available. On modern the smallest detectable IC (0.0551) exceeds the IC required to be tradeable (~0.04-0.05), and pooling more history is inadmissible under Amendment D5, which admits 0 of 11 estimates because signal properties are not stable across eras even where instrument properties are. Eleven candidate signals were measured and the largest was |t| 1.56 against a 2.19 bar. Two hypotheses registered, two killed, both on signal rather than plumbing.
futures_trend.reopen_requires: Either (a) a dataset that lifts the smallest detectable IC materially below 0.04 within a SINGLE era — a longer modern era, higher-frequency observations, or a materially wider universe — or (b) a signal class whose IC is pre-registered and then measured above 0.05 on modern alone, without pooling. Section 7 allows no extensions, so either route is a charter amendment rather than a registration.

index_structures.grounds: No edge was demonstrated, and the question WAS resolvable — this is the strong form of closure, not the resolvability form used for futures_trend. Two structures spanning the family's gamma range (iron butterfly with ATM shorts, iron condor with delta-0.18 shorts a median 6.8 intervals out) were each entered unconditionally on weekly NIFTY across the full modern era, each supplied an A5-sized sample (179 and 198 trades, ~50/year against A5's 32.3), and each lost: expectancy -Rs 705 and -Rs 406/trade, t -1.95 and -1.44, both NEGATIVE BEFORE FRICTION (gross -84,720 and -41,858). The +2.38 vol point VRP measured here is real and is payment for the left tail, not a mispricing: strip the 10 worst of the condor's 198 weeks and the book is +Rs 55,851, which is the short-vol payoff working as designed and losing anyway. The arena's other routes are separately closed — vanilla credit spreads excluded by Section 8, the calendar killed as cal-cheapvol-modern with its term structure measured flat at -0.00020 variance units (t -0.14), the reverse calendar measured and not worth building, and ratios unsizeable without an undefined-risk sizing rule that does not exist.
index_structures.reopen_requires: A structure in this arena that is NOT short volatility -- the two kills cover the short-vol family from ATM to 0.18-delta shorts and say nothing about long-vol or dispersion structures. Concretely: evidence that a long-gamma or relative-value index-option structure clears Section 4's bar on a sample A5 can use, OR a demonstration that the -2.38 vol point premium inverts in some identifiable and tradeable regime (not a regime filter fitted to these same 377 trades, which Section 6.3 forbids). A different wing width, delta target or exit rule on the SAME short-vol structures is a retry, not a reopening, and Section 7 does not permit it.

event_vol.grounds: No edge was demonstrated, and the question WAS resolvable — the strong form, as for index_structures. EARNINGS HALF: the volatility premium was MEASURED, not merely searched for. Across 246 single-stock earnings events in the modern era the mid-price P&L of a short ATM straddle is -Rs 174/trade, indistinguishable from zero; the -Rs 3,857/trade realised loss is bid-ask, not mispricing. Because a buyer pays the same spread, both directions are negative at EVERY slippage level INCLUDING ZERO, where the long side collects the +174 mid premium and still loses to statutory friction alone (Rs 311/trade). That robustness matters: slippage_per_leg=0.75 is an assumption, not a measurement, and this conclusion does not rest on it. The result is also structure-independent — a cheaper two-legged structure has nothing to recover from a premium of approximately zero. Three hypotheses closed (evol-earnings-modern, evol-earnings-pre2024, evol-earnings-narrowwing), the last with 246 trades at t = -9.08 and a MONOTONE wing sweep in which more sample is uniformly more loss. Capacity, once the true constraint was identified (a self-imposed risk cap at 45% of refusals, not market illiquidity at 12%), was fixed and is not the reason for closure. MACRO HALF: unregistrable against A5 by arithmetic — roughly 40 events in one liquidity era cannot reach 100 OOS trades by any route, even with a perfect calendar, and the calendar cannot be sourced anyway (FOMC parses 8-for-11 years, RBI's archive is ASP.NET postback-driven with no stable URL).
event_vol.reopen_requires: An event-vol structure whose edge does NOT depend on the straddle premium that was measured at zero here — the -Rs 174/trade mid-price figure covers ATM straddles with wings on the 60 most-liquid F&O names at 2-days-before / 1-day-after timing, and says nothing about skew, term structure across the event, or single-leg directional announcement drift (which is arguably cross_sectional, not this arena). Concretely: a measurement showing a non-zero MID-PRICE premium on some event-vol structure, taken on data other than these same 246 events, since fitting a subset or a timing to them is Section 6.3. A different wing, universe, or entry timing on the same short straddle is a retry, which Section 7 does not permit. The macro half additionally requires a verifiable RBI/Budget source AND a route to 100+ OOS events that does not exist at ~40 events per era.

cross_sectional.grounds: No edge was demonstrated, and the SEARCH BUDGET is exhausted rather than the question being exhaustively answered — this is a weaker closure than index_structures or event_vol, and is stated as such. What was measured: T2b scored eleven candidate signals (momentum at four lookbacks, reversal at two, low-vol, 52-week high, acceleration, OI change, volume trend) and nothing cleared — largest |rank IC| 0.0359, and NEGATIVE; largest |t| 1.56 against a 2.19 eleven-signal bar. xsect-mom-modern registered 12-1 momentum and died at t +0.13, with its own signal measured at rank IC -0.0139. This arena's remaining open condition was explicitly that it NOT be searched further: one pre-registered signal, because detectable IC is 0.0249 for one candidate but 0.0463 when fishing across eleven, against a required 0.054 — so a twelfth search would itself close the arena by spending the detectability margin. That one signal was spent on cross-sectional carry (annualised futures basis), declared with its direction and thresholds in ARENAS.md X1 and COMMITTED BEFORE COMPUTATION. It is refuted: rank IC -0.0270, t -2.22, 41 rebalances, 95% CI [-0.0508, -0.0032] against a required +0.0540 — wrong sign, entire CI below zero, and detectable (|IC| 0.0270 > the 0.0249 this sample can distinguish). The pre-declaration barred re-reading a negative result as 'short high carry works'. Data limitation recorded: UndrlygPric is empty for stock futures before 2024, so carry is computable on 2024+ only; this cannot change the verdict, because a positive pre-2024 estimate would fail D5.1 sign consistency and D1 would return the decision to a negative modern.
cross_sectional.reopen_requires: More rebalances, or a signal class this arena has not seen. Two concrete routes. (1) POWER: the binding number is 41 rebalances at a 15-trading-day horizon. UndrlygPric becoming available pre-2024, or a calendar-spread estimator of the same curve slope validated against the 2024+ figures, would roughly triple the sample and move detectable IC below 0.02 — but note D5.1 blocks any pooled estimate whose per-era signs disagree, so this only helps if the added history agrees with modern. (2) A GENUINELY NEW SIGNAL CLASS: everything tested is a function of past returns, volume, open interest, or the futures curve. Fundamentals (value, quality, accruals), borrow/short-interest data proper rather than its basis proxy, analyst revisions, and index-inclusion flow are all untouched and none is derivable from bhavcopy — each needs a data source this project does not have. Acquiring one of those is the honest reopening condition. A further lookback, weighting or horizon on the signals already scored is a retry, which Section 7 does not permit, and would in any case spend the detectability margin the arena no longer has.
